title: Chemistry
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Measure with units and significant figures, explain atomic structure, periodic trends and bonding, name compounds, use moles and stoichiometry, and study gases, solutions, acids, bases, rates and equilibrium.

weeks.3: Electron configuration and the periodic table

blocks.deliverable: Convert units by dimensional analysis with correct significant figures.
Predict ionic or covalent bonding from electronegativity.
Convert between grams, moles and particles.
Week 7 midterm; find a limiting reagent and percent yield.
Prepare a dilution plan from a stock solution.
Compute pH and predict a shift with Le Chatelier's principle.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Kitchen titration: estimate the acetic acid content of vinegar with baking soda, or analyze a supplied titration data set, and report the result with its uncertainty.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
